heroHeadline: Trump Brokers 3-Day Ceasefire (May 9–11) as Both Sides Keep Firing — Russia Kills Civilians in Chernihiv; Ukraine Strikes Yaroslavl Refinery
heroSubtitle: On May 9, President Trump announced both Zelensky and Putin agreed to a US-brokered 3-day ceasefire running May 9–11, with a 1,000-for-1,000 prisoner-of-war exchange — the largest of the war. Trump called it 'the beginning of the end.' Within hours, both sides accused each other of violations: Russia launched 1 Iskander-M ballistic missile and 43 drones at Ukraine, killing a father and son in Chernihiv region at an agricultural enterprise. Russia's Defense Ministry counter-claimed 8,970 Ukrainian ceasefire violations (including 7,151 drone strikes) — figures dismissed by Western analysts. Ukraine struck a Yaroslavl oil refinery (Slavneft-YANOS, ~1,000 km inside Russia) and targets near Rostov-on-Don on the night of the ceasefire announcement. Zelensky issued a satirical 'decree' formally excluding the exact military grid coordinates of Moscow's Red Square from Ukraine's targeting plan during Victory Day parade hours — a pointed demonstration of Ukraine's reach. Russia's Victory Day parade (May 9) proceeded without military vehicles for the first time since 2007; only Slovakia's Fico and Belarus's Lukashenko attended among foreign leaders. The ceasefire follows Russia's total failure to observe previous ceasefires: on the prior Ukrainian ceasefire (May 5–6), Russia violated it with 108 drones and 3 missiles, killing 22 Ukrainians. ISW confirmed Russia suffered a net territorial loss of 116 sq km in April 2026 — first net loss since the Kursk incursion.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OHCHR, ISW, CSIS, Ukrainian MoD, US DoD, NATO, IAEA, EU Council, UK MoD, and major news outlets including Reuters, BBC, AP, Al Jazeera, Bloomberg, Kyiv Independent, Euronews, NPR, CBC, and RBC-Ukraine. Casualty figures are estimates; Russia has never released official figures.
